Rashi on Eruvin 28a:10:1.english: Median clover - The sweet clover of Media is of good quality.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:11:1.hebrew: כשות - הומלין. בבבל אוכלין חזיז, וכי אתא רב לבבל וחזא דאכלי להו — אמר מערבין, ומעיקרא אמר דאין מערבין:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:11:1.english: Dodder - Hops [homlon]. In Babylonia they eat green grain; and when Rav came to Babylonia and saw that they ate it, he said that one may establish an eiruv [with it], whereas initially he said that one may not establish an eiruv [with it].

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:1.english: For greens - To eat [them] in their green state.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:2.hebrew: זרען חייב - במעשר, ואע"פ שלא זרען מתחילה לכך:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:2.english: Their seed is obligated - In tithes, even though he did not initially sow them for this.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:3.english: And their greens are exempt - For it is of no consequence.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:5.hebrew: הגרגיר - אורוגא, נאכל בין זרע ובין ירק:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:13:5.english: The arugula - Orugue [rocket] — it is eaten both [as] seed and [as] an herb.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:14:1.english: When Rav said - That one may establish an eiruv with them:

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:1.hebrew: פוטיתא - שרץ המים קטן שאין בו כזית, ואפ"ה, כיון דבריה היא — אכילה היא, ולוקה ד' מלקיות: בשרץ המים, כתיב בתורת כהנים: ״אל תשקצו את נפשותיכם בכל השרץ השורץ ולא תטמאו בהם״ — הרי כאן שנים, וכלל בהן בין שרץ הארץ בין שרץ המים; ומשום ״מבשרם לא תאכלו״; ומשום ״וכל אשר אין לו סנפיר וקשקשת לא תאכלו״:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:1.english: Putita - A small water-creature that does not have [the volume of] an olive-bulk; and even so, since it is a whole creature [beriyah], it is [considered a full act of] eating, and he incurs four [sets of] lashes: Regarding a water-creature, it is written in Torat Kohanim [Leviticus]: “You shall not make yourselves detestable with any swarming creature that swarms, neither shall you make yourselves unclean with them” — behold, here are two [prohibitions], and He included in them both the swarming creature of the earth and the swarming creature of the water; and on account of: “Of their flesh you shall not eat”; and on account of: “And whatever does not have fins and scales you shall not eat.”

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:2.hebrew: נמלה - שהוא שרץ הארץ, לוקה ה': תרתי — הא דאמרן; "וכל הולך על גחון לכל השרץ השורץ על הארץ לא תאכלום" — הרי ג'; "וכל השרץ השורץ על הארץ שקץ הוא לא יאכל" — הרי ד'; "ולא תטמאו את נפשותיכם בכל השרץ הרומש על הארץ" — הרי ה'. כולן בפרשת ויהי ביום השמיני:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:2.english: An ant - Since it is a creeping creature of the earth, [one who eats it] incurs five [sets of lashes]: Two [are] that which we said; "Whatever goes on its belly... among all creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat them" — behold, three; "And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth is a detestable thing; it shall not be eaten" — behold, four; and "neither shall you defile your souls with any creeping thing that moves upon the earth" — behold, five. All of them [are] in the Torah portion of Vayehi BaYom HaShemini.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:3.hebrew: צרעה לוקה שש - שהיא שרץ העוף, ולקי בכל הני חמשה, מוסף עליו: "וכל שרץ העוף שקץ הוא לא יאכל" במשנה תורה. והאי דכתיב בקדושים תהיו: "ולא תשקצו את נפשותיכ' בבהמה ובעוף ובכל אשר תרמוש" — לא חשיב ליה, דבבהמה וחיה ועוף גדולים משתעי, ולא בשרצים, דלא כתיב בהו "שרץ". לשון שרץ — דבר שהוא נד בארץ, ואינו נראה אלא ע"י שירוצו וריחושו, מפני קוטנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:3.english: A hornet, he is given six - For it is a winged swarming creature, and he is lashed for all those five [prohibitions], with [an additional one] added to it: "And every winged swarming creature is detestable; it shall not be eaten" [Deuteronomy 14:19], in Mishneh Torah. And as for that which is written in [the parashah of] Kedoshim Tihyu: "And you shall not make your souls detestable with beast, or with fowl, or with anything wherewith the ground teems" [Leviticus 20:25] — he did not count it, because it speaks of large domesticated beasts, wild animals, and birds, and not of swarming creatures, as "swarming creature" is not written in it. The term "swarming creature" [refers to] a thing that moves on the ground and is not visible except through its scurrying and creeping, on account of its smallness.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:4.hebrew: ואם איתא - דדגים גידולי קרקע נינהו, "פוטיתא נמי לילקי משום שרץ הארץ" גרס, ולא גרס "לילקי ה'", דשבע בעי למילקי — חמש דשרץ הארץ ושתים דשרץ המים:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:1:4.english: And if it is so - That fish are products of the ground — the reading is: “[One who eats] a putita should also be lashed on account of the creeping thing of the earth,” and the reading is not: “He should be lashed five [times],” for he would need to be lashed seven [times]: five for the creeping thing of the earth and two for the creeping thing of the water.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:4:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דמאן דמרבי עופות קסבר - כל היכא דאיכא כלל ופרט וכלל, כללא בתרא עיקר, ובתריה אזלינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:4:1.english: What is the reason of the one who includes fowl? He holds - Wherever there is a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, the latter generalization is primary, and we follow it.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:4:2.hebrew: והוה ליה פרט וכלל ונעשה כלל מוסיף על הפרט ומרבי כל מילי - וכללא קמא — דאתי למעוטי ולמימר דנדרשי' בכלל ופרט, ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, ולא נרבי מידי — לא אזלינן בתריה. ומיהו, אהני פורתא למימר דכי מרבי כללא בתרא, לא כל מילי מרבי, אלא כעין הפרט — מאי דדמי ליה מב' צדדין, דהוי פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע. ומיתרבי נמי עופות בהאי דינא, ולמעוטי דגים, דלא דמו ליה אלא בחד צד — בפרי מפרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:4:2.english: And it is [treated as] a detail and a generalization, and the generalization is considered an addition to the detail and includes everything - And as for the first generalization — which comes to restrict [the scope] and to say that we should expound it as a generalization and a detail, [meaning that] “there is in the generalization only what is in the detail” and we should not include anything — we do not follow it. However, it was somewhat effective [in leading us] to say that when the latter generalization includes [items], it does not include everything, but rather [only items] similar to the detail — whatever resembles it in two respects: that it is produce of produce and grows from the ground. And fowl are also included under this rule, and [this serves] to exclude fish, which resemble it in only one respect — in [being] produce of produce.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:5:1.hebrew: ומאן דממעט עופות קסבר - כל היכא דאיכא כלל ופרט, כללא קמא דווקא, ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, וממעטי כל מילי, ואפי' מאי דדמי ליה בפרטא. והדר כתב כללא בתרא לאפוקי ממיעוטא דכללא קמא במקצת, ולאתויי מיהא מידי דדמי לפרטא בכל ג' צדדין — דהוי פרי מפרי, וגידולי קרקע, וולד ולדות הארץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:5:1.english: And the one who excludes fowl holds - Wherever there is a generalization and a detail [followed by another generalization], the first generalization is primary, and the generalization includes only that which is in the detail, and all [other] things are excluded, even that which is similar to it in the detail. And then [the Torah] wrote the latter generalization to remove [items] from the exclusion of the first generalization in part, and to at least include anything that is similar to the detail in all three respects — that it is produce of produce, and grown from the ground, and offspring of the offspring of the earth.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:1.hebrew: פעפועין - ירקות שקורין קקול"י בל' ארמי, יוטלי"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:1.english: Pefo’in - Vegetables that are called kakule in the Aramaic language, [and] joteles [beet greens] in Old French.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:2.english: Purslane - Polpier in the vernacular [Old French for purslane].

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:4.hebrew: חזיז - שחת של תבואה כשהוא ירק, וגוזזין ואוכלין אותו:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:4.english: Green grain - Forage of grain when it is green, and they cut and eat it.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:6:5.english: Unripe dates - Inferior dates that have not fully ripened.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:7:2.hebrew: ואם הוקשו - הקלחין כעץ, שכבר צמח בהן זרעו — קשין הקלחין לכל אדם:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:7:2.english: And if they hardened - [If] the stalks [become] like wood, as their seed has already grown in them — the stalks are harmful to all people.

Rashi on Eruvin 28a:8:1.hebrew: תרגמא - להא דאמר רב מערבין — אשלא הוקשו, וזה המערב בהן יש לו בנים, דהשתא חזו ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 28a:8:1.english: Interpret it - [Apply] that which Rav said, “One may establish an eiruv,” to [those] that have not hardened; and this [person] who establishes an eiruv with them has children, so that now they are fit for him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:1.hebrew: ובבל הויא רובא דעלמא והתניא כו' - תימה: אמאי לא משני כדמשני בפ' חבית (שבת קמד, ב): "מי דמי? ערביא — אתרא, הכא — בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם"? וי"ל, דהתם ודאי שייך לחלק: דכולי עלמא נמי אם היו להם גמלים הרבה כמו בערביא — היו מקיימין קוצים בשדותיהן, ולכך יש חשיבות באתרא. אבל בית מנשיא, אע"פ שכל העולם נמי אם היו להם רמונים היו סוחטין — כיון דלא הוי אלא חד גברא, בטלה דעתו. אבל הכא, שבכל העולם יש חזיז ולא אכלי — אין לחלק בין אתרא לגברא. ולהכי נמי לקמן (עירובין דף כט:) דפריך: "ופרסאי הוו רובא דעלמא?", ולא מייתי מהך ברייתא דליבטלו פרסאי לגבי רובא דעלמא — דאין לי לבטלם, כיון דרוב בשר יש להם, ושאר העולם נמי אם הוי להם רוב בשר היו אוכלים בלא לחם, דומיא דערביא; ומייתי שפיר מבגדי עניים, דלא בעי שיעור עשירים כיון שפחות חשוב בעיניהן, ועוד דמדמי השיעורים להדדי; ולא שייך נמי לאתויי לקמן ההיא דחבית: [וע"ע תוס' שבת צב: ד"ה ואת"ל]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:1.english: "Is Babylonia the majority of the world? And wasn't it taught, etc." - [This is] puzzling: Why does [the Gemara] not answer as it answers in the chapter [entitled] Ḥavit (Shabbat 144b): "Are [these cases] comparable? Arabia is [an entire] region; here, [an individual's] opinion is nullified relative to all [other] people"? And one can say that there, it is certainly appropriate to distinguish [between an entire region and an individual], for everyone [else] in the world as well, if they had many camels as [they do] in Arabia, would maintain thorns in their fields; and therefore, there is significance to [the practice of] a region. However, [regarding the practice of] the house of Menashya, even though everyone in the world as well, if they had pomegranates [in abundance], would squeeze [them], since he was only a single individual, his opinion is nullified. But here, where young green shoots [ḥaziz] exist throughout the entire world and yet [people] do not eat [them], there is no [reason] to distinguish between a region and an individual. And for this reason as well, later on (Eruvin 29b), where [the Gemara] challenges: "And are the Persians the majority of the world?", and it does not cite this baraita [to argue] that the Persians should be nullified relative to the majority of the world — because I cannot nullify them, since they have an abundance of meat, and the rest of the world as well, if they had an abundance of meat, would eat [it] without bread, similar to [the case of] Arabia; and [therefore] it rightly cites [the mishnah regarding] the garments of the poor, which do not require the measure of [the garments of] the wealthy since a lesser [measure] is significant to them; and furthermore, because [the Gemara there] compares the measures to one another. And it was also not applicable to cite later on that [distinction] of [the chapter] Ḥavit. [And see further, Tosafot, Shabbat 92b, s.v. Ve'im timtzei lomar.]

Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:2.hebrew: לפיכך זרען חייב וירקן פטור - אין להקשות: מאי "לפיכך"? הא קתני דבטלה דעתו! דאיכא למימר: בטלה דעתו לענין דמתעשר אחר הבאת שליש כדין זרע, או לענין תורם מן הרעה על היפה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:2.english: "Therefore, their seeds are obligated and their greens are exempt" - One should not object: What is [the purpose of] "Therefore" — doesn't it [already] teach that his intention is nullified? For one can say: "His intention is nullified" [could have been understood as applying only] with regard to it being tithed after reaching a third [of its growth], in accordance with the law of seeds, or with regard to one who separates terumah from the inferior for the superior.

Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:3.hebrew: לזרע מתעשרין זרע וירק - תימה: אמאי לא עירב ותני להו, "זרען לזרע או לירק — מתעשרין זרע וירק"? ואומר ר"י, דהיכא דזרען לירק — הוי ירק עיקר, ומתעשר הכל אחר לקיטה כירק, בין ירק בין זרע; ואם זרע לזרע — מתעשר הכל לשעבר אחר זמן הראוי למעשר זרע, ולא בתר לקיטה. ולהכי תנא ברישא "ירק וזרע" ובסיפא "זרע וירק" — דברישא ירק עיקר, ובסיפא זרע עיקר. ונפקא מינה נמי לעניין מן הרעה על היפה: דכשירק עיקר הוי ירק יפה, וכשזרע עיקר הוי זרע יפה, והוי מן הזרע על הירק מן היפה על הרעה. וכן משמע בירושלמי בפרק [רביעי] דמעשרות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:13:3.english: "[If he sowed them] for seed, they are tithed seed and herb" - It is puzzling: Why did [the Tanna] not combine and teach them [together]: "If he sowed them for seed or for herb, they are tithed seed and herb"? And the Ri explains that where he sowed them for herb, the herb is primary, and everything is tithed following the harvest like an herb, whether herb or seed; but if he sowed [them] for seed, everything is tithed retroactively according to the time appropriate for the tithing of seed, and not following the harvest. And that is why [the Tanna] taught in the first clause "herb and seed" and in the latter clause "seed and herb" — for in the first clause the herb is primary, and in the latter clause the seed is primary. And there is also a practical difference with regard to [the rule of not tithing] from the inferior for the superior: for when the herb is primary, the herb is [considered] the superior [quality], and when the seed is primary, the seed is [considered] the superior [quality], and [tithing] from the seed for the herb is [tithing] from the superior for the inferior. And so it is indicated in the Yerushalmi in the [fourth] chapter of Ma'asrot.

Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:1:1.hebrew: צירעה לוקה שש - פי' בקונט', דהא דכתיב בקדושים "לא תשקצו וגו' ובכל אשר תרמש האדמה" — בגדולים משתעי, דלא כתיב "שרץ". וקשה, דבפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נט:) דרשינן: "ובכל חיה הרומשת" — זה נחש; משמע דרמישה נמי הוי דבר הרוחש, כמו נחש ההולך על גחונו! ומפרש ה"ר יעקב דאורלינ"ש, דבמעילה פרק קדשי מזבח (מעילה דף טז:) מוקי האי קרא דוקא בשמונה שרצים, כדכתיב "אשר הבדלתי לכם לטמא" — במובדלין דבר הכתוב:
Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:1:1.english: A hornet is given six [sets of lashes] - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that that which is written in [Parashat] Kedoshim: "You shall not make your souls detestable... and with all that creeps upon the ground" (Leviticus 20:25), speaks of large [creatures], for it does not write "creeping thing" [sheretz]. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59b), we expound: "And with every animal that creeps" (Genesis 1:28) — this is the serpent; which implies that "creeping" [remishah] is also a crawling thing, like a serpent that goes on its belly! And Rabbi Yaakov of Orléans explains that in Me'ilah, in the chapter [entitled] Kodshei Mizbe'ach (Me'ilah 16b), [the Gemara] establishes this verse specifically with regard to the eight creeping animals [sheratzim], as it is written: "Which I have set apart for you to defile" (Leviticus 20:25) — the verse speaks of those that are distinguished [to transmit ritual impurity].

Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:4:1.hebrew: אהני כללא קמא למעוטי כל דלא דמי ליה משני צדדים - וא"ת, דבנזיר בפ' ג' מינין (נזיר דף לה:) אמר: מאי איכא בין תרי פרטי וכללא לתרי כללי ופרטא? תרי כללי ופרטא, אי איכא דדמי ליה אפי' בחד צד — מרבינן; תרי פרטי וכללא — עד דדמי ליה משני צדדין. משמע דבחד צד סגי! וי"ל, דשני צדדין דהכא הוי כחד צד דהתם, דשני צדדין פרי מפרי וגידולי קרקע שוין הן. ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף כד:) גבי שן ועין דריש: מה הפרט מפורש מומין שבגלוי ואינו חוזר — הא נמי צדדין שוין. והא דפריך התם למימר: מה הפרט מפורש מומין שבגלוי ובטל ממלאכה ואינו חוזר — היינו למאן דאמר כללא קמא דווקא, דע"כ צד דבטל ממלאכתו גרוע מהנך, מדקמשני: "לחפשי ישלחנו" ריבויא הוא; ואם שוה הוא, אמאי מרבינן ליה טפי משאר צדדין? וכי האי סוגיא איתא בחולין (דף סו.) בסוף אלו טריפות גבי ארבה, ובריש אלו מומין (בכורות דף לז.) גבי פסח או עור, ואתו כולהו כמאן דאמר כללא קמא דווקא, כדפירש'. ועוד אומר ר"י, דאתא שפיר אפי' למ"ד כללא בתרא דווקא, ולדידיה נמי צריך שידמה בכל צדדין החשובין, אע"פ שהא' חשוב מחבירו, רק שלא יהיה צד גרוע יותר מדאי; אבל למאן דאמר כללא קמא דוקא, מצריך שיהא דומה אף בצד גרוע הרבה. והדבר מסור לחכמים להכיר איזהו צד גרוע שחולקין בו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 28a:4:1.english: The first generalization is effective in excluding anything that is not similar to it in two respects - And if you say: In Nazir, in the chapter entitled Sheloshah Minim (Nazir 35b), the Gemara asks: What is the difference between two details and a generalization, and two generalizations and a detail? And it answers: In the case of two generalizations and a detail, if there is an item that is similar to it even in a single respect, we include it; whereas in the case of two details and a generalization, we do not include it until it is similar to it in two respects. This implies that for two generalizations and a detail, being similar in a single respect is sufficient! And one can say: The two respects here are considered like a single respect there, as the two respects — "the produce of produce" and "growing from the ground" — are equal. And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (24b), regarding tooth and eye, the Gemara expounds: Just as the detail is explicit as being blemishes that are exposed and do not regenerate — these, too, are equal respects. And that which the Gemara objects there to say: Just as the detail is explicit as being blemishes that are exposed, and caused a cessation from work, and do not regenerate — that is according to the one who says that the first generalization is primary; for perforce, the aspect of causing a cessation from his work is inferior to those other two, since the Gemara answers that "he shall let him go free" is an inclusion; and if it were equal, why would we include it more than the other respects? And a discussion like this one is found in Chullin (66a), at the end of the chapter entitled Ellu Tereifot, regarding locusts; and at the beginning of the chapter entitled Ellu Mumin (Bekhorot 37a), regarding a lame or blind animal; and they all follow the one who says that the first generalization is primary, as we explained. And furthermore, the Ri says: It works out well even according to the one who says that the latter generalization is primary, and according to his opinion, it must also be similar in all significant respects, even though one is more significant than the other, provided that it is not an excessively inferior respect; whereas according to the one who says that the first generalization is primary, he requires that it be similar even in a very inferior respect. And the matter is given over to the Sages to discern which is the inferior respect over which they disagree.
